lines: A frightened flock scatters. A frightened village nearly does too. You helped gather us.
I can mend torn wool. Mending a village takes people who show up.
You helped keep panic from scattering everyone beyond reach.
The village needed gathering, and your courage gave us a center.
I saw people find their doors because the raiders were forced back.
A safe fold matters most when the night is loud.
You helped bring the village through frightened but together.
Some courage is quiet afterward. I see it anyway.
You held the road long enough for us to get the children inside.
The raiders never reached the pens because you drew them away.
I saw you turn back for a villager who had fallen.
Your warning gave us time to bar the doors.
The bell stopped ringing only after you cleared the square.
We still lost walls and windows, but fewer names are missing from the count.
You stood where the gate broke and did not let fear move you.
The flock settles when danger leaves. People take a little longer.
I will remember who carried the wounded after the fighting.
You gave the healers a chance to work without another attack.
The village owes you more than cheers at the well.
When the repairs are done, your part in this will still matter.
